## **Understanding the Foundation: HIPAA and Your Medical Records Release Form in Raleigh**


### **Key Elements of a Valid HIPAA Authorization**


A compliant authorization under[45 CFR 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) generally has to include a specific set of elements, and providers will reject forms that miss them. The rule itself calls for:


-


A meaningful description of the information to be used or disclosed, including record types and dates of service


-


Identification of who may disclose the protected health information, meaning the specific facility or department


-


Identification of who may receive it, meaning your firm and the attorney of record


-


The purpose of the disclosure, which may be stated as "at the request of the individual" when the patient initiates the authorization


-


An expiration date or expiration event, such as resolution of the legal claim


-


The patient's signature and the date signed, plus a description of a representative's authority if someone signs on the patient's behalf


-


Required statements covering the right to revoke in writing, the prohibition on conditioning treatment or payment on signing, and the possibility that redisclosed information may no longer be protected by HIPAA


Individual facilities often ask for more than the rule strictly requires. Many Raleigh providers want a date of birth, current address, or partial Social Security number for identity matching, along with the fax number and department for routing. Those are operational requirements set by the facility, not federal ones, so check the form you are actually submitting.


### **Common Pitfalls to Avoid with Release Forms**


Authorization rejections delay your case timeline significantly. Watch for these issues:


-


**Missing sensitive information checkboxes** : mental health, substance use, HIV/AIDS, genetic testing, and sexually transmitted disease records commonly require explicit authorization beyond a standard release


-


**Unclear expiration dates** : many facilities reject forms without specific expiration language


-


**Electronic signature rejection** : some Raleigh facilities still require original handwritten signatures


-


**Incomplete provider information** : a wrong facility name or a missing department designation causes routing failures


Incomplete or defective authorizations are one of the most common preventable causes of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can send a request back and restart the provider's processing timeline.[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, incorrect provider information, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.

## **Beyond the Basics: Accessing Old and Online Medical Records in Raleigh**


### **Leveraging Connected Retrieval Channels**


Codes Health reaches records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone outreach, which helps locate documentation across fragmented treatment histories. That matters when a client cannot recall every treatment location or when care was spread across unrelated systems.


### **Strategies for Locating Records from Closed Practices**


When a provider has closed, retired, or merged, record custody depends on the particular practice, its owner, any successor organization, and the applicable retention rules. Reasonable places to start:


-


The former practice's successor, or whoever acquired the patient panel


-


A hospital system that absorbed the outpatient practice


-


Third-party storage companies contracted for retention compliance


-


The provider's professional liability carrier, estate, or designated custodian


[The North Carolina Medical Board's](https://www.ncmedboard.org/resources-information/professional-resources/laws-rules-position-statements/position-statements/medical-records-documentation-electronic-health-records-access-and-retentio) position statement on record retention advises physicians to keep adult records for at least 11 years and records for minors until the patient turns 30. Licensing boards can point you toward guidance, but they do not take possession of medical records and should not be treated as a locator service.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can a Raleigh personal injury lawyer request medical records without a HIPAA authorization?**


Generally no. Under[45 CFR 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) , providers cannot release protected health information for litigation purposes without a valid patient authorization. HIPAA does allow disclosure in response to certain judicial and administrative processes, including court orders and subpoenas that satisfy the rule's notice or protective order conditions, but those pathways depend on an existing proceeding and the applicable procedural authority. That is why authorization-based requests are the standard tool during pre-litigation investigation.


### **What are the most common reasons a medical record request gets denied by Raleigh providers?**


Incomplete or defective authorizations are the most common preventable cause. Specific issues include missing patient signatures, unclear or missing expiration dates, failure to check boxes authorizing release of sensitive information such as mental health or substance use records, incorrect facility names or addresses, and missing date ranges. Some facilities also reject electronic signatures and require an original handwritten authorization.


### **Are there specific fees associated with requesting medical records from Raleigh hospitals?**


Yes. NC General Statute § 90-411 permits providers to charge up to $0.75 per page for the first 25 pages, $0.50 per page for pages 26 through 100, and $0.25 per page thereafter, with a $10 minimum fee. Additional charges may include search and handling fees, actual mailing costs, certification fees, and imaging media costs for CDs. Costs vary by provider and record volume, so verify the current schedule before budgeting a case.


### **How do pre-existing conditions affect medical record requests for personal injury cases?**


Pre-existing conditions call for records predating the incident, typically two to three years prior. That documentation establishes baseline function and lets experts separate injury-related damages from prior conditions. Opposing counsel will obtain these records during litigation anyway, so pulling them early supports realistic case evaluation and settlement strategy.


### **What happens if a healthcare provider fails to respond within the HIPAA deadline?**


HIPAA's 30-calendar-day response requirement, with one permitted 30-day extension on written notice, applies to an individual's right-of-access request. Attorney requests made under a patient authorization are a separate mechanism, and timing follows provider policy and applicable state law. When a provider stalls, document every follow-up attempt. Access-rights complaints can be filed with the HHS Office for Civil Rights, and in active litigation, subpoenas and sanctions provide additional leverage.
